findings.claim: Writing `at: today` as a bare date does not clear a concept or docs page whose source changed today. as_datetime reads a bare date as its UTC midnight, and review_due flags `source changed` when the source's last commit time is later than verified_at. So a person who checks a concept the same day its source changed runs kmctl verify, gets exit 0, and the id is still listed. That breaks the plan's core promise (the id leaves kmctl review due). For a docs page it is the common case, since a docs page is never due for `unverified`, only for stale_after or a changed source. The plan should write a full UTC datetime (OKF dates are ISO 8601 datetimes since v0.2, and generated.at already uses them), and r1/r2 should include a source committed earlier the same day.

A verified entry does not clear the `stale_after passed` reason, yet the plan's new Next: line in kmctl review due points at kmctl verify whenever anything is due, and the done-when says verify makes review due stop listing the id. An agent sent by that line to verify a concept or docs page that is due for stale_after runs the verb and the id stays due. That is the same dead end the operator reported. The plan has to choose: verify also moves or clears stale_after (one more input and its rule), or the Next: line and the verb's help say verify clears only `unverified` and `source changed`, and name the fix for stale_after. r6 and r1/r2 should test whichever is chosen.

A bare-date verified at reads as midnight UTC, so a source committed earlier the same day kept the id due. The plan now writes a full UTC timestamp in the _STAMP form (seconds, Z), and r1 and r2 test the same-day case.

A verified entry never clears stale_after passed. The plan now adds --stale-after (the stale_after_time forms), requires it when stale_after has passed, and the review due Next: line names it for that reason; r4 and r4b test both sides.

A CRLF file is rewritten with LF on every line. verify reads with path.read_text (universal newlines, so 
 becomes 
) and writes with path.write_text, so every line of the file changes, against the plan's 'leaves every other line of the file as it was' and the docs' 'changes no other line'. Probe: '---
type: note
...---

# a
' comes back all-LF. No test covers a CRLF file.

_target accepts '..' segments as long as the resolved path stays under its base, and the handoff check runs on the raw id, not the resolved path. 'decisions/../handoffs/h' and 'docs/../.okf/handoffs/h' both verify a handoff (exit 0, verified entry written), and 'docs/../README' writes a verified entry into README.md, since the docs base is the whole repository root. The id and the log line then carry the '..' form. Check the handoff case and the docs/ prefix on the resolved path (or refuse '..' and absolute parts), and add a refuses case for it.

docs/reference/commands.md's exit-code list omits two refusals the verb has: a --stale-after that is not in the future, and a verified field in a form it cannot extend. The text output line also omits the 'stale_after is now ...' line printed with --stale-after.

A trailing comment on the verified line ('verified:  # checks' over a block list, or 'verified: []  # none') makes _with_entry refuse, telling the person to rewrite it as a block list it already is. Strip a trailing ' #...' comment from rest before classifying it, or name the comment in the refusal.

entries.change: Reads and writes bytes and keeps the file's CRLF or LF line ending; _target refuses an id holding .. or an absolute path, and resolves docs/ ids under docs/ instead of the repository root.
Adds a CRLF keeps-line-endings test and refuses cases for decisions/../handoffs/..., docs/../.okf/handoffs/... and docs/../README.
The verify exit-code list names the not-in-the-future and cannot-extend refusals and ids holding ..; the output line names the stale_after line.
